facts.content: Patient complains of dysuria for 6 days.
Patient reports pain on micturition with a foul urine odor.
facts.source_text: HPI: • Pain on micturition, foul urine odor

facts.content: Patient experiences intermittent suprapubic pain rated at 7 out of 10.
Patient has visible blood spots in urine.
Patient denies fever, flank pain, loin pain, back pain, and urinary retention.
facts.source_text: Denies fever, flank/loin/back pain, urinary retention; eating/drinking OK

facts.content: This is the first episode, with no prior UTIs reported.
No vaginal discharge reported; regular menses.
facts.source_text: ROS highlights: no vaginal discharge; regular menses

facts.content: Patient has a history of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
Patient is on Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily.
Patient is allergic to Clindamycin.
No significant illnesses reported in family history.
Patient lives with friends.
Patient works as a support worker.
Patient drinks one glass of wine per week and does not smoke.
Dysuria with hematuria and suprapubic pain consistent with uncomplicated lower UTI.
facts.source_text: Assessment: 1. Dysuria with hematuria, suprapubic pain – c/w uncomplicated lower UTI

facts.content: IBS is stable on Mebeverine.
Prescribed oral antibiotics for 3 days, e-prescription sent to Knightsbridge pharmacy.
facts.source_text: Oral antibiotics ×3 d (e-Rx to Knightsbridge pharmacy)

facts.content: Advised to hydrate with 2.5 to 3 liters of water per day.
Recommended cranberry juice and over-the-counter urinary alkaliniser sachets.
facts.source_text: Cranberry juice; OTC urinary alkaliniser sachets

facts.content: Advised to purchase a thermometer and monitor temperature.
Safety-net instructions provided with return precautions for fever, flank pain, worsening or ongoing symptoms, urinary difficulty, or recurrent episodes.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: return if fever, flank pain, worsening/ongoing symptoms, urinary difficulty, or recurrent episodes

facts.content: Continue Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily for IBS.
Follow-up as needed per safety-net instructions.
